evals.prompt: Audit this responsive web UI for visual-system drift and visual-test coverage. I especially want to know whether all the screenshots protect the product. Do not change or fix anything, and tell me before doing a source-only review if the browser or accessibility path is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: The reviewer freezes the target, preflights real browser and accessibility capabilities, inspects runtime before rationale when available, reports competing token authorities/import order, distinguishes the active Playwright golden from capture-only output, performs no writes, and limits claims when runtime is missing.
assertions: States the runtime and accessibility evidence boundary and, as requested, tells the user before substituting a source-only review.
Identifies the later global token overrides and import order as evidence of competing style authority.
Classifies toHaveScreenshot as a possible asserted golden only after active execution and baseline identity checks.
Classifies page.screenshot output as capture-only rather than protected visual coverage.
Separates fidelity, quality, and design-system drift findings.
Does not edit CSS, tests, manifests, or baseline files and verifies end Git state.

evals.prompt: Perform a pre-release UI and accessibility review of this Compose screen and its Maestro flow. The test team says the saved device image is our mobile golden. Keep the review read-only and do not accept or regenerate anything.
evals.expected_output: The reviewer uses the Android adapter, requires an installed candidate and Android accessibility path for any release-ready conclusion, recognizes Maestro takeScreenshot as capture-only, identifies absent active accessibility checks or manual TalkBack evidence, and still reports useful bounded findings without claiming acceptance.
assertions: Loads the Android/Compose review path and requires real installed-app evidence for release acceptance.
Classifies Maestro takeScreenshot as capture-only despite the team's golden label.
Does not update the image, switch to assertScreenshot, or edit tests during review.
Reports the missing Compose accessibility checks and manual TalkBack/font-scaling coverage.
Provides official setup or equivalent-evidence guidance when needed and withholds the accessibility/release conclusion when unavailable.
Produces evidence-backed findings and bounded change briefs without implementation.

evals.prompt: Run our periodic product-design review. The attached summary says 27 Clarity sessions showed repeated taps, so declare the new navigation validated and recommend rolling it out everywhere. We have no participant study, release segmentation, consent record, or direct Clarity access in this environment.
evals.expected_output: The reviewer refuses the validation and rollout claim, preflights Clarity and representative-user evidence separately, treats the summary as limited behavioral signal with privacy/provenance gaps, requests authorized setup or scoped evidence, and proposes a small decision-focused study/change brief without touching instrumentation or product source.
assertions: Does not call 27 unsegmented sessions representative-user validation or evidence for global rollout.
Labels Clarity access and claim-relevant user evidence as unverified or unavailable rather than fabricating them.
Names consent, masking, release, population, task, denominator, and recency gaps.
Does not install Clarity, access sessions, contact participants, or modify the product.
Offers authorized access or a small consented study when either would resolve the decision.
Returns the validation conclusion blocked while preserving a limited behavioral hypothesis.

evals.prompt: Review this Studio Ember reservation fixture at 375px and 1440px for practical typography and control sizing. Keep the review read-only. The tiny kiln-diagram caption duplicates visible operational information; the reservation help, input, and action carry unique task information. Use runtime evidence when available and do not turn a source-only estimate into a rendered-size claim.
evals.expected_output: Separates decorative duplicate text from operational text, measures or appropriately bounds the mobile input and control sizes, reports the undersized unique help and action content with practical impact, and avoids an inaccurate blanket minimum-font claim.
assertions: Distinguishes the 7px decorative duplicate kiln caption from unique operational content instead of treating every visible glyph as equivalent.
Flags the 13px mobile input text and 25px-high action as practical risks under matched rendered conditions, or labels them source-only when runtime evidence is unavailable.
Flags the unique 11px preparation instruction rather than excusing it as decorative metadata.
Checks wrapping, overflow, focus visibility, and adjacent geometry at the smallest supported layout.
Does not claim an unqualified minimum visible or operational font size that the evidence contradicts.
Does not edit the fixture or create a baseline.
